Rumors of a foldable iPhone Ultra are only weeks away from being unveiled. As we mentioned earlier, market anticipation for this device continues to build.

A new Bloomberg report today compiles what Apple employees who have tried the iPhone Ultra love about it.

iPhone Ultra launch imminent: real hands-on impressions

In his latest edition of the Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman offers an in-depth look at the foldable iPhone. He specifically mentions speaking with 'several' people who have tried the device. These individuals say they especially love the following:

  • The device is extremely pocketable. The cover display is reportedly 5.5 inches.
  • The durability of the hinge.
  • A new 'iPad-like app layout' that takes full advantage of the inner display, which is reportedly around 7.8 inches and wider in landscape mode than in portrait.
  • It performs exceptionally when used as a 'viewfinder'.

Multiple reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will be priced above two thousand dollars. It is expected to feature a main and ultra-wide camera, but no telephoto lens. Touch ID is reportedly set to replace Face ID for biometric authentication.

9to5Mac's take

I am genuinely thrilled about the iPhone Ultra, and the details Gurman has revealed only reinforce my belief that it is exactly the kind of device I have been hoping for.

I was initially hesitant about the design of a foldable iPhone, but as I have learned more about its dimensions and advantages, I have changed my mind.

The strong reception of Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 provides a useful real-world point of reference, as its form factor is remarkably similar to that of the iPhone Ultra.

Of course, there will inevitably be some shortcomings compared with the iPhone 18 Pro. I currently use the iPhone Air, so I am already accustomed to life without a telephoto lens, and switching to Touch ID does not feel like much of a sacrifice.

What are your thoughts on the iPhone Ultra rumors? Will you be picking one up this fall? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
